title: Factorized depth × expert codes over a global reused pool
hypothesis: A shared expert pool with a factorized depth×expert functional coordinate generalizes to unseen layer-expert combinations with fewer complete bytes than independent role experts while preserving routing balance.
physical_object: eight global 8×8 experts reused at eight layer depths
mirror_coordinate: rank-2 product of depth factors and expert factors over shared matrix bases
logical_multiplicity: 64 layer-expert functions from eight physical experts and rank-2 role factors
controls: MoRE-style additive depth plus expert embeddings

development.selection_metric: heldout role operator/output nRMSE, complete serialized bytes, active compute and per-layer expert load balance

fresh.reason: exact native bilinear attribution is evaluated before any fresh role access

grid.heldout_roles: checkerboard rule (layer + expert) mod 4 == 0; all rows and columns retain six training pairs

storage.authority: actual compressed NPZ inference payload bytes

success_gate: Heldout routed output nRMSE <=0.02, per-layer top-1 load max/min <=1.25, >=25% fewer complete bytes than independent roles, and strict frontier improvement over additive and native bilinear controls.
failure_gate: FAIL for Mirror-specific value if native bilinear exactly matches state/function or if quality, bytes, compute, or load-balance gates miss.
boundaries: Synthetic linear experts and fixed balanced per-layer router only; no trained MoRE/UniPool, language-model NLL, or GPU throughput claim.
Heldout roles are omitted from shared basis and factor fitting; this is synthetic role-composition generalization, not fresh model checkpoints.
Per-role operator weights are oracle generated from a rank-2 bilinear teacher; factor fitting uses observed role matrices.
